title: The Invitation
sceneText:
Early in the morning a messenger rides over from Millridge with a formally worded letter.

The wax carries the Duke’s arms: the hunting season is a duchy occasion and the invitation goes out in the duchy’s form. But the writing inside is in Baron Henk’s own hand, broad and open, less an order to a subordinate than an invitation between neighbours. Maplegate’s previous steward took part in the season every year, and he hopes the custom will hold.

“The camp is pitched at the hunting ground on the east side of the ducal woods. Opening this afternoon, five days, until sundown on the twenty-second of October.”

Gregor puts his head out of the stable.

“That letter comes every year.” He commits to nothing either way. “Mr Hartmann attended seven years running. From the eighth he found reasons not to.”

There is a line appended at the foot of the letter, in smaller and looser writing than the body:

“Her Grace the Duke will be present at the opening this year.”

Gregor glances at that line.

“Her Grace comes every year,” he says. “She has never once come over to our side.”

effects.logEntry: You changed into riding dress and went to the ducal hunting ground after noon.

choices.text: Send back a properly worded apology

effects.logEntry: You wrote an apology and sent it back with the messenger.

choices.resultText:
You write a reply. You take a while over the wording: the harvest is at its height, the estate is short of hands, with regrets, and next year without fail.

You give it to the messenger to take back. He looks at you as he takes it — the look holds some surprise — but he says nothing.

Gregor is standing in the stable doorway.

“Answered it?”

You say you did.

“Mm.”

He turns and goes in. You do not know whether he approves.

Three days later you hear at the market that eleven men came to the opening this year. Other years it is twelve.

choices.text: Make no answer, and get on with the estate

effects.logEntry: You did not answer the letter from Millridge.

choices.resultText:
You put the letter on the desk and go and see to other things.

The messenger waited in the courtyard for nearly an hour. Martha brought him water. In the end he left on his own.

At dusk Martha asked, in the kitchen, whether the letter from Millridge wanted answering.

You said no.

She said “oh”, and did not ask again.
